parts.text: For Examiner’s Use In this laboratory investigation, you will investigate the cooling of water by four different methods. You are provided with a supply of hot water. Experiment A (cooling with stirring ).

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Pour approximately 200 cm 3 of the hot water supplied into beaker 1 . Place the thermometer in the beaker of water. When the thermometer reading stops rising, record the temperature θ 1 . θ 1 = .......................................................

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Start the stopclock and stir the water for one minute. Record the temperature θ 2 of the water. θ 2 = .......................................................

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the temperature difference ( θ 1 – θ 2 ). ( θ 1 – θ 2 ) = ...................................................... [3] Experiment B (cooling with pouring ).

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) Empty beaker 1 . Pour approximately 200 cm 3 of the hot water supplied into beaker 2 . Place the thermometer in the beaker of water. When the thermometer reading stops rising, record the temperature θ 3 . θ 3 = .......................................................

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Remove the thermometer. Carefully pour the water from beaker 2 into beaker 1 . Pour the water back into beaker 2 . Repeat this process four times.

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Place the thermometer in the beaker of water. Record the temperature θ 4 of the water. θ 4 = .......................................................

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate the temperature difference ( θ 3 – θ 4 ). ( θ 3 – θ 4 ) = ....................................................... [1] Experiment C (cooling with a lid ) and Experiment D (cooling without a lid ).

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Pour approximately 200 cm 3 of the hot water supplied into beaker 1 . Place the thermometer in the beaker of water. When the thermometer reading stops rising, record the temperature θ 5 . θ 5 = .......................................................

parts.label: iii
parts.text: For Examiner’s Use (iii) Pour approximately 200 cm 3 of the hot water supplied into beaker 2 . Place the thermometer in the beaker of water. When the thermometer reading stops rising, measure the temperature θ 6 . θ 6 = .......................................................

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Place the lid on beaker 1 . Start the stopclock. Allow both beakers to cool for 3 minutes.

parts.label: v
parts.text: (v) At the end of the 3 minute cooling period, record the temperature θ 7 of the water in beaker 1 and the temperature θ 8 of the water in beaker 2 . θ 7 = ....................................................... θ 8 = .......................................................

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) If this laboratory investigation is to be repeated many times to check the results, suggest one condition that should be kept constant in order to provide reliable results. .....................................................................................................................................
